 De la Fuente Defends Lamine Yamal and Confirms New Injury Concern for Spain
 Luis de la Fuente has defended Lamine Yamal and confirmed that Aymeric Laporte is doubtful for the match against Czech Republic. The Spain head coach faces a crucial UEFA Nations League fixture with several fitness concerns.
 Laporte Raises Concerns Ahead of Czech Republic Clash
 The Spain national team have arrived in Prague with a new defensive concern.
 Just hours before facing Czech Republic in the fifth round of the UEFA Nations League , Luis de la Fuente confirmed that Aymeric Laporte is dealing with a viral illness that prevented him from taking part in the final training session.
 The Athletic Club defender was unable to train alongside his teammates at Letná Stadium, and his availability for Thursday's match will depend on how his condition develops over the next few hours.
 His potential absence represents a problem for the head coach, who could be forced to make changes to his defensive lineup.
 If Laporte is unavailable, players such as Pau Cubarsí and Dean Huijsen could emerge as alternatives in central defense.
 However, De la Fuente has yet to confirm his starting lineup.
 The situation has forced the coaching staff to take precautions, particularly with Spain also preparing to face England on Sunday.
 De la Fuente Responds to Criticism Over Lamine Yamal
 In addition to Laporte's situation, the Spain head coach was questioned about Lamine Yamal's absence against the Czechs.
 The Barcelona winger is continuing his recovery after finishing the match against Atlético de Madrid with discomfort in his right knee.
 Medical examinations revealed inflammation and fluid buildup in the joint, prompting the coaching staff to allow him to continue his treatment in Barcelona.
 However, criticism suggesting that the youngster was receiving special treatment prompted a firm response from De la Fuente .
 "Lamine has no special privileges. We would have done the same for any other player," the manager stated during his press conference.
 The Spain head coach also expressed his frustration with reports questioning how his players' medical situations are handled, reiterating that every decision is made with their well-being in mind.
 Lamine Yamal could join the national team camp on Friday if his recovery continues to progress positively, with the aim of being available against England .
 The situation is similar to that of Mikel Oyarzabal , who also did not travel to Prague due to a bout of flu.

 Spain Aim to Enter England Showdown as Group Leaders
 Despite the absences, Luis de la Fuente does not want his players to lose sight of their immediate objective.
 Spain head into the match against Czech Republic with four victories from four matches and a perfect 12 points.
 The Spanish national team have already secured qualification for the UEFA Nations League quarterfinals, but they still need to defend first place in their group.
 Next Sunday, they will host England at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid, in a match that could determine who finishes top of the standings.
 However, the head coach made it clear that he has no intention of holding anything back against the Czechs because of what might happen three days later.
 For De la Fuente , securing victory in Prague is essential to entering the final group-stage fixture with the biggest possible advantage.
 The match also presents an opportunity for players who usually have fewer minutes to demonstrate that they can step up when injuries and absences affect the squad.
 La Roja have built their impressive form on collective strength, a quality the manager considers essential to maintaining their competitive level.
 With Laporte struggling with illness and Lamine Yamal still recovering, Spain will have to prove that they have enough depth to overcome another challenge.
 The objective is clear: conquer Prague, maintain their perfect record, and enter the showdown against England with control of the group in their hands.
 Key Takeaways From Luis de la Fuente's Comments
 Aymeric Laporte is doubtful for the match against Czech Republic due to a viral illness that prevented him from participating in Spain's final training session.
 Luis de la Fuente defended Lamine Yamal , insisting that the Barcelona winger receives no special treatment within the national team.
 Spain have won four consecutive matches in the UEFA Nations League and are looking to maintain their lead before hosting England on Sunday, November 15.
